source.version: Undated author manuscript marked UNDER PEER REVIEW, with printed pages matching PDF pages. The retrieval and citation records identify this saved document as PsyArXiv preprint tbvq2_v1, DOI 10.31234/osf.io/tbvq2_v1, posted 2026-07-03. The document itself does not print that posting date or version identifier. The ACM version of record was not available for comparison.
source.supplement_used: Appendix A, Experimental Platform and Paradigm (PDF pp. 33-37, including Tables A1-A3), and Appendix B, Additional Results (PDF pp. 38-42), bound into the same PDF. No separate supplement on file was identified.

studies.label: Agency instructions with AI access, or human-only control, on the Alternative Uses Task

counts_source.quote: external constraints on recruitment duration resulted in a final sample of N = 150. ... high-agency (N = 12) and low-agency (N = 10) conditions ... were therefore excluded from the final analyses.

arms.name: High-Agency
arms.description: Access to the custom chatbot; instructed to expand upon their own ideas with AI and generate even more creative ideas (PDF p. 11; Figure A1, PDF p. 33).

arms.name: Low-Agency
arms.description: Access to the same chatbot; instructed to let AI generate creative ideas and use its suggestions directly, with AI doing the heavy lifting (PDF p. 11; Figure A1, PDF p. 33).

arms.name: Control (human only)
arms.description: Same Alternative Uses Task without a chatbot; explicitly told not to use AI, with copy-paste disabled (PDF p. 11; Figure A1, PDF p. 33).

studies.task: Community college students generated five non-standard uses for each of brick, bubble wrap, and frisbee during one session; object order was counterbalanced (PDF pp. 11-12).

ai_tool.name: gpt-3.5 (custom chatbot embedded in a Qualtrics survey)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 11, Submission Phase; PDF p. 33, Appendix A, Web App and Language Model. No release year or dated model snapshot is stated.

preregistration.where: PDF p. 10, Preregistration: https://osf.io/2d7fe/overview?view_only=c34f80bd046e4c85aafdee3d2c33a74e; hypotheses on PDF p. 9; deviations on PDF p. 14.
preregistration.primary_outcome: H1: externally rated overall creativity, originality, and usefulness; H2: group-level homogeneity assessed by similarity to the condition-object centroid. The paper calls these its primary hypotheses and the centroid analysis preregistered; the clustering analysis is exploratory.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Third-party U.S. adult evaluators recruited via CloudResearch Connect rated submitted alternative uses, using the rubric in Table A1. The evaluator scale endpoints are not explicitly stated in the methods. The self-rating scale is a separate measure. Overall impression of cleverness, ingenuity, innovation, and a surprisingly good solution.

stats.difference_is: Printed regression coefficient is control minus treatment (Control (human only) minus Low-Agency); its sign is retained as printed.

regression.model: Linear mixed-effects model fitted with lme4; condition is the fixed effect, with random intercepts for submitters and objects. Low-Agency is the reference level. The printed Control coefficient is Control (human only) minus Low-Agency: control minus treatment in this extraction record. The paper does not separately name the SE estimator.

sources.locator: PDF p. 17, Homogeneity, permutation-test definition
sources.quote: we conducted permutation tests (n = 5,000 permutations) comparing the maximum and minimum condition means for each metric.

estimates.notes: The reported statistic is the maximum minus minimum of condition means, with the Results identifying the two extreme conditions. The permutation p-value tests that maximum-minus-minimum statistic, not a separately documented prespecified pairwise test. Condition means, their SDs/SEs, numerical confidence limits, analyzed people by arm, and the number of analyzed sets are not printed. The resampling unit is not described; se_basis is conservatively set to set because the reported analysis compares condition/object clustering metrics and does not establish participant-level uncertainty. Figure 3 displays t-SNE cluster maps, not numerically labeled arm metrics. The same printed observed difference is stored in difference and test.value because it is also the permutation-test statistic; these are not independent estimates.

sources.locator: PDF p. 17, Homogeneity, permutation-test definition
sources.quote: we conducted permutation tests (n = 5,000 permutations) comparing the maximum and minimum condition means for each metric.

estimates.notes: The reported statistic is the maximum minus minimum of condition means, with the Results identifying the two extreme conditions. The permutation p-value tests that maximum-minus-minimum statistic, not a separately documented prespecified pairwise test. Condition means, their SDs/SEs, numerical confidence limits, analyzed people by arm, and the number of analyzed sets are not printed. The resampling unit is not described; se_basis is conservatively set to set because the reported analysis compares condition/object clustering metrics and does not establish participant-level uncertainty. Figure 3 displays t-SNE cluster maps, not numerically labeled arm metrics. The same printed observed difference is stored in difference and test.value because it is also the permutation-test statistic; these are not independent estimates.

estimates.outcome: Coefficient of variation of HDBSCAN cluster sizes
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Exploratory HDBSCAN clustering of sentence embeddings separately by condition and object. The paper does not specify the embedding model for this particular analysis or whether it includes all submitted or only sampled ideas. Standard deviation of cluster sizes divided by mean cluster size; higher values indicate more imbalance and concentration in a dominant category, interpreted as greater homogeneity.

open_items: The ACM proceedings version of record could not be compared with the saved preprint. Python urllib requests to the ACM PDF and then the Crossref API failed with a socket-access restriction; no newer text was retrieved.

The number randomized is not printed. PDF p. 10 reports a submitter sample and additional attention-check exclusions, but the timing relative to assignment is not specified. All study and arm randomized counts remain null.

The total number of people analyzed, analyzed people in each arm/contrast, and retained trials by arm are not printed. The recruitment/final-sample count is not the outcome-model sample after noncompliance exclusions. No analyzed count was computed by subtraction or from degrees of freedom.
The sample to which the idea-data-logging exclusions on PDF p. 10 apply is not explicitly named. Placement after the evaluator description is insufficient to resolve it.

No observed arm means, arm SDs, or numerical arm-mean confidence limits are printed for the eligible outcomes. Model intercepts, random-effect SDs, and residual SDs in Tables A2-A3 are not observed arm levels/SDs. Participant-level standardizers remain unavailable.

Table A2 uses Low-Agency as reference. Control coefficients therefore run control minus treatment in the AI-versus-control records. High-Agency-versus-Control coefficients, SEs, and raw differences are not printed and have not been reconstructed.

The collective prose p-value bound for creativity/originality does not reconcile cleanly with Table A2. Tabulated Low-Agency-versus-Control coefficients/SEs are retained; their prose bound is documented in notes. High-Agency-versus-Control records retain the only printed bound with its collective provenance.
The prose usefulness result lacks a comparator and conflicts with Table A2, the abstract, and the Discussion. It requires clarification before assignment to a contrast.

The homogeneity methods give cosine distance, while Table A3, Figure 2, and the Results interpretation use cosine similarity. Extraction follows the reported/visualized similarity outcome and explicitly preserves the formula conflict.

The centroid pool and clustering inputs are not fully specified. The clustering paragraphs do not name the embedding model, and the permutation procedure does not identify its resampling unit. Its set-based uncertainty must not be assumed participant-level.
The Discussion claims a CV difference between the AI conditions, but no corresponding numerical test or pairwise effect is printed. That comparison remains a qualitative record.
The evaluator rating endpoints are not explicitly stated; the self-rating scale is separately described. Figure 1 also has a caption referring to cosine similarity despite showing rating outcomes.
The setting is not explicitly identified as remote or supervised. online_rct follows the screening form provisionally; the individual random assignment is explicit regardless of setting.
The paper names gpt-3.5 but gives no release year or dated model snapshot. ai_tool.year remains null rather than using the paper year or an inferred model-release year.
notes: Extracted independently as B on 2026-10-10 from the saved PDF, after reading the entire markdown conversion including references and both appendices. All numerical estimate fields were checked against PyMuPDF text on the cited PDF pages; Tables A2-A3 were also recovered with find_tables using text strategies, and the main figures and experimental-paradigm image were inspected. Printed precision and minus signs are preserved in the source quotes; JSON numeric values are transcriptions, with no effect, count, mean, SD, CI, or p-value calculated. The paper reports N = 150 submitters (PDF pp. 10 and 14), but excludes noncompliant object trials and entirely excludes High-Agency and Low-Agency participants; that number is not entered as n_analyzed. These are the paper’s full reported treatment comparisons after its compliance exclusions, not intention-to-treat estimates. Outcome-model uncertainty that includes submitter random intercepts is coded participant; the exploratory clustering permutation tests lack a documented participant-level resampling basis. For AI-design contrasts High-Agency is the tested agency-supporting intervention and Low-Agency its default/delegation comparator, consistent with the primary hypotheses (PDF p. 9). Both AI arms use open chat. No combined-AI-versus-control contrast is printed. The screening form identifies no other paper sharing these participants. Self-ratings and process measures are excluded; the omnibus homogeneity test and unassigned usefulness result are documented without assigning them to a pair. No other file was written.
